_meta.description: Structured discovery canvases. Each canvas defines a set of boxes (text fields), a quality checklist, and reflection prompts.

canvases.title: Customer Discovery Canvas
canvases.subtitle: Problem discovery: does the problem exist, and does it actually matter?

boxes.title: Customer Segment
boxes.desc: Role, context, and geography of the person you're talking to.

boxes.title: Learning Goals
boxes.desc: What must this interview confirm or invalidate?

boxes.title: Evidence of Pain
boxes.desc: Direct evidence (what they did, when, what it cost). Not interpretation.

boxes.title: Existing Solutions
boxes.desc: Manual workarounds, spreadsheets, or vendors they currently use.

boxes.title: Exact Quotes
boxes.desc: Verbatim phrases. Avoid paraphrase.

boxes.title: Next Step
boxes.desc: End with a hard judgment: pursue, pivot, kill.

checklist: Started with their workflow, not my idea.
Asked for a specific recent example, not opinions.
Captured at least one verbatim quote.
Got a commitment (next meeting, intro, or deposit).
reflections: Is the pain tied to a recurring operational reality?
Who feels the pain directly vs indirectly?
What would convince you this segment is wrong?

canvases.title: Interview Synthesis Canvas
canvases.subtitle: Pattern recognition: what repeated across interviews, what broke your assumptions?

boxes.title: Repeated Patterns
boxes.desc: Themes that showed up in 3+ interviews.

boxes.title: Contradictions
boxes.desc: What didn't fit? Why?

boxes.title: Customer Language
boxes.desc: Words and phrases to shape positioning and copy.

boxes.title: Working Decision
boxes.desc: Proceed / pivot / stop. With reasons.

checklist: Compared notes across interviews, not just the latest one.
Separated recurring evidence from one-off anecdotes.
Used exact customer language, not my own framing.
reflections: Which patterns are strong enough to act on?
What evidence is still too thin to trust?
What's the next experiment that would resolve the biggest unknown?

canvases.title: Value Proposition Canvas
canvases.subtitle: Match what you build to what the customer is trying to get done.

boxes.title: Customer Jobs
boxes.desc: The functional, social, or emotional jobs they hire a solution to do.

boxes.title: Pains
boxes.desc: Frustrations, blockers, and risks in their current path.

boxes.title: Gains
boxes.desc: Outcomes and benefits they want — required, expected, desired.

boxes.title: Products & Services
boxes.desc: What you offer (features, capabilities).

boxes.title: Pain Relievers
boxes.desc: How your offering eliminates specific pains.

boxes.title: Gain Creators
boxes.desc: How your offering produces the gains they want.

checklist: Each pain reliever maps to a specific customer pain.
Each gain creator maps to a specific customer gain.
I can name a customer who would say 'yes' to each row.
reflections: Which pain reliever is the strongest reason to switch from the status quo?
Where am I solving a problem the customer doesn't actually have?

canvases.title: Riskiest Assumption Test
canvases.subtitle: Find the one thing that, if wrong, kills the business — and design a cheap test for it.

boxes.title: The Assumption
boxes.desc: State it as a falsifiable claim.

boxes.title: Why It's Risky
boxes.desc: What collapses if this is wrong?

boxes.title: Evidence Today
boxes.desc: What do you know now? What's only opinion?

boxes.title: The Test
boxes.desc: Cheapest experiment that would invalidate it.

boxes.title: Pass / Fail Metric
boxes.desc: Specific number, before you run the test.

boxes.title: Result & Decision
boxes.desc: What you learned. Persevere, pivot, or kill.

checklist: The assumption is falsifiable, not vague.
I set the pass/fail metric before running the test.
The test runs in under 2 weeks.
I know what I'll do with each possible outcome.
reflections: Am I testing the riskiest thing, or the easiest thing to test?
What would I do tomorrow if this came back negative?
